name: STORMVEIN DYNAMICS Pelagic Series IV Aqua Leg
product_name: Stormvein Dynamics Pelagic Series IV Aquatic Leg
description:
The Pelagic Series IV is a bilateral full leg replacement designed for sustained aquatic operation, featuring a hydrodynamically contoured shell that reduces drag by 40% compared to biological legs in open water. Each foot houses a deployable composite swim fin that extends on command via a wrist-tap or neural trigger, retracting flush for land use without visible protrusion. An internal pressure compensation system equalizes joint cavity pressure at depths up to 120 meters, preventing the joint seizure that destroys standard cyberlimbs at depth.

Stormvein's Pelagic line serves the Great Lakes diving industry, underwater infrastructure maintenance crews, and the small but intensely dedicated community of competitive open-water swimmers who work the Lake Michigan depth circuit. In Meridian 88's waterfront districts, the distinctive matte-blue hydrodynamic shell of a Pelagic user is immediately recognizable — and carries significant professional credibility in aquatic trades.
installation_requirements: Stormvein-certified aquatic prosthetics clinic, pressure calibration dive required post-installation, bilateral installation mandatory for hydrodynamic function
rejection_risk: Low — Stormvein's pressure-equalized nerve coupler reduces inflammation at depth, well-tested in commercial diving populations
maintenance: Fin mechanism lubrication monthly, pressure compensation calibration every 6 months, full depth-test certification annually for commercial diving use

cultural_context: Stormvein's waterfront presence in Meridian 88 is substantial — the company maintains a dedicated service center in the Port District and sponsors the annual Lake Michigan Depth Circuit, an open-water endurance race that doubles as a product showcase. Pelagic users in the diving trades form tight professional networks, and being able to display the Stormvein serial plate is informally considered proof of serious aquatic credentials.

Port District salvage and recovery operatives
story_hooks: A Pelagic Series IV user was the last person seen near a sunken cargo container that's now the center of a territorial dispute between two waterfront factions — and their pressure logs from that dive are encrypted.
Stormvein's annual depth circuit has been infiltrated: someone swapped a competitor's fin deployment firmware with a version that will lock the fins extended mid-race, potentially fatal at depth.

An underwater infrastructure crew using Pelagic legs has gone silent 80 meters below the lake surface — their last telemetry showed normal vitals, but something cut their comms exactly 12 minutes into the dive.
